A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DisTime and InternVid-TG research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A-E are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original DisTime benchmark evaluations, component and dataset ablations, annotation-quality measurements, and qualitative predictions in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations, annotation-quality measurements, and qualitative predictions reported in v1.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same single time token, distribution-based decoder, Gaussian time encoder, iterative re-encoding, and training losses. The InternVid-TG annotation pipeline is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Training coverage in Table 2 and evaluation coverage in Section 5.2 and Appendix C are unchanged. Both evaluate moment retrieval, dense captioning, grounded video QA, and general video understanding on the same datasets, with the same InternVid-TG-1k annotation-quality evaluation.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 4-8 and appendix Tables A and D, after matching renumbered citations. The four newly cited temporal-action works are not added to the reported experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: Both versions report the same metrics, training budgets, model sizes, and evaluation settings, including 16-frame InternVL inputs, at most 32-frame LLaVA-OneVision inputs, and zero-shot Charades-STA and QVHighlights evaluation. Appendix training settings and analysis sample sizes also match.

E4.justification: The distribution/re-encoding and training-data ablations in Tables 3-4 are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same ensemble, bin-count, and layer-count analyses, while Appendix E retains the same temporal-distribution illustration and qualitative cases.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The temporal probability distributions and confidence-score analysis remain unchanged and do not introduce experimental uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and rankings in Tables 3-8 and A-D match, as do the qualitative findings. For example, DisTime-InternVL-8B retains 81.0 Charades-STA R@1 at IoU 0.3, and the annotation ensemble retains 43.97 mIoU.

T1.justification: The normalized timestamp definitions, anchor-weighted decoding, Gaussian encoding, Equations 1-6, and combined training objective are unchanged. No mathematical derivation, theorem, or proof is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: lightweight continuous-time representation, automated InternVid-TG construction with 179k videos and 1.25M events, improved temporal-task performance, and competitive general video QA.

C2.justification: The explanations and applicability boundaries remain the same, including incompatibility with global temporal aggregation, the possible effect of fewer frames on ANet-Caption captioning, and difficulties recalling multiple QVHighlights segments for one event.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the explicit statement 'Code and data are released' with 'DisTime is released' at the same repository URL, making the availability disclosure less specific. Implementation details, training settings, hardware, timing, and instruction templates remain unchanged; actual resource availability changes are not established.

R1.justification: v2 adds four references to the introductory temporal-task discussion: DeTAL, ReAct, TriDet, and 'Temporal action localization with enhanced instant discriminability.' These expand background citations without substantively changing the related-work discussion or novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited wording edits in the abstract, annotation description, implementation details, and benchmark paragraph. The narrative, section order, and appendix organization remain unchanged; most apparent textual movement results from repagination.

P2.justification: Existing diagrams and tables are resized or more tightly spaced and repositioned. For example, Tables 1, 3, 4, and 8 move earlier, and the conclusion fits on page 8. The same figures, tables, and appendix visualizations are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 adds background citations and makes modest wording and layout adjustments, while retaining the same scientific arguments, results, ablations, and limitations. The release statement becomes slightly less explicit. These limited changes leave the paper's overall scientific support and reproducibility essentially unchanged.
